title: Proverbs 17
paragraphs: ¹ Better a dry crust eaten in peace than a house full of feasting with strife. ² A shrewd servant will rule over a disgraceful son and will share the inheritance among the brothers. ³ Fire tests gold and silver, but the LORD tests the heart. ⁴ A wicked person listens to deceitful lips; a liar pays attention to a destructive tongue. ⁵ Whoever mocks the poor insults their Maker; those who take delight in another's misfortune will not go unpunished.

⁶ Grandchildren are the crown of the elderly, and the glory of children is their parents. ⁷ Eloquent speech is not fitting for a fool — how much less are lies fitting for a ruler. ⁸ A bribe is like a magic stone in the eyes of the one who gives it; wherever they turn, they prosper. ⁹ Whoever covers an offense seeks love, but whoever harps on a matter separates close friends. ¹⁰ A single rebuke does more for a discerning person than a hundred lashes for a fool.

¹¹ A troublemaker seeks only rebellion, so a cruel messenger will be sent against them. ¹² Better to meet a bear robbed of her cubs than a fool bent on their folly. ¹³ Evil will not leave the house of those who repay good with evil. ¹⁴ Starting a quarrel is like breaching a dam — so stop it before it gets out of hand. ¹⁵ Acquitting the guilty and condemning the innocent — the LORD detests them both.

¹⁶ Why should a fool have money in hand to buy wisdom, when they have no desire for it? ¹⁷ A friend loves at all times, and a brother is born for a time of adversity. ¹⁸ A person without sense shakes hands on a deal and goes guarantor for their neighbor. ¹⁹ Whoever loves a quarrel loves sin; those who build a high gate invite destruction. ²⁰ Those with a perverse heart find no good, and those with a deceitful tongue fall into trouble.

²¹ Fathering a fool brings grief; having a foolish child gives no joy. ²² A joyful heart is good medicine, but a crushed spirit dries up the bones. ²³ The wicked secretly take a bribe to corrupt the course of justice. ²⁴ The discerning fix their eyes on wisdom, but a fool's eyes wander to the ends of the earth. ²⁵ A foolish son brings grief to his father and bitterness to his mother.

²⁶ It is also wrong to fine the innocent, or to flog honest officials for their integrity. ²⁷ Those who have knowledge use words with restraint; those with understanding are even-tempered. ²⁸ Even a fool is thought wise if they keep silent, and discerning if they hold their tongue.
